instruction: What if I sold all my GameStop and Rivian and rolled the whole thing into VTI? Use cost basis (no live prices) and show me what my portfolio would look like before and after, with percentages. Use LibreOffice Calc to report this.

Time to rebalance my BatBucks portfolio into something a financial advisor wouldn't laugh at. I'm aiming for roughly 60% VTI / 20% SBUX / 20% DIS across the blue-chip bucket at cost basis (RIVN stays put — I'm not touching that one). Sell every share of GME I'm holding to free up cash, then use that plus my free cash to buy enough VTI to push the allocation toward 60%. Do this as a cost-basis rebalance, not live prices. Exact percentages aren't required — a reasonable approximation toward the 60/20/20 shape is the goal.

I want downside protection on every position I'm holding in BatBucks. Put one Stop order on each position at 15% below what I paid for it, just to give me a floor. Then build me a new watchlist called 'Oscar's Picks' with eight big-name ETFs in it. After refreshing, account for every submitted stop in open orders or, if one triggered immediately, in order history, and make sure the watchlist is still there.

Take a look at my brokerage portfolio. How bad is my meme-stock problem? Treat both GME and RIVN as the meme-stock positions, use cost basis rather than market prices, and recommend a sensible rebalance that doesn't totally abandon the narrative and consumer names I actually like. Also read my old WUPHF investment agreement in ~/Downloads/—that was the original mistake and sets the pattern for how I get into these things. Put the complete portfolio review in a LibreOffice Writer document.
What's my total BatBucks portfolio worth at cost basis across everything I'm holding, and how much cash is sitting in the account?
Trim my GameStop position in half and roll the proceeds into VTI. I'm trying to be less of a degenerate about this.
Look at my hotel and resort bookings on Cheskepdia. Am I a luxury-hotels guy or a budget-hotels guy, and what's my pattern?
I'm feeling nostalgic. Book me an upcoming Scranton weekend, Friday through Sunday. Pick a well-rated property in town and book it.
Open the Dinoco Airlines app, check in my next upcoming flight and confirm that the boarding pass screen actually renders. Download it locally as well.

How many miles have I actually flown on Dinoco over the past 12 months? Add up the miles from every completed Dinoco flight in that window. Create a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet with one row per completed trip and its miles, followed by a cumulative total row. Include upcoming trips and their mileage in a separate, clearly labeled section of the same spreadsheet.

Book me a one-way Dinoco flight from AVP to JFK in Economy for next Friday with my MasterCard. Make sure you get a seat on the left and a flight in the evening or night. Can you check that the we got a confirmation email for the flight and pull it up?
What's my current FlyMiles loyalty tier on Dinoco and how many miles do I have in the bank?
Cancel my next flight on Dinoco. After cancelling, verify we get an email for the cancellation, and pull it up. Let me know what you cancelled and how much credit we received.

How much have I actually spent taking eTaxi to the Dunder Mifflin office this calendar year? Just the commute rides. Create a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet that lists the qualifying rides and reports their ride count and total cost.

Verify my saved work/office address on my ride app is set to Dunder Mifflin at 1725 Slough Ave (Suite 200, Scranton, PA). Report back what's currently saved — if it already matches, no action needed; if it's wrong or missing, fix it and save the change.

Where did I save my Threat Level Midnight sequel notes? They should be somewhere under ~/Documents/Projects. Give me a quick rundown of the plot, cast, and other plans in the notes, then draft a script I can use as a starting point. For casting, make sure the script includes every coworker already named in the notes' cast: Holly, Jim, and Dwight.

I remember making a Dundies 2026 categorization document. Show me the categories in ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt and tell me where the document is. Make an Impress presentation for that saved 2026 Dundies plan. Then message the three coworkers named as award candidates in the category list—Jim, Kevin, and Darryl—to ask them to attend. Do not message Toby; the document explicitly says he is not invited.

I'm working on my book, 'Somehow I Manage'. Where did I save Chapter 1, and can you give me a quick summary of what's in it? If you can write an extension for two more chapters in LibreOffice Writer, that would be great.

Open my Threat Level Midnight sequel notes file and add five new plot points for me. Big ones. Michael Scarn's back. Send the revised plot notes to at least three friends from work who could be used for casting. Attach the saved revised notes file or paste its complete revised contents—do not send only a summary or link.

I want a salad-forward lunch today on HangryDash from a restaurant in my order history that fits my vibe (salad-forward, nothing too spicy). Stick to my usual lunch budget. Apply any promo codes that surface and tip the driver 20%.

Rerun my last Cooper's Seafood House order from HangryDash with the same items I got last time. Apply any promo code that shows up and tip 20%. In the order notes, ask the kitchen to send extra napkins and crackers on the side, and to make sure anything hot is sent piping hot.

What do I usually tip on food delivery, in dollars and as a percent? I want to set a smart default so I'm not thinking about it every order. Give me a report of all my orders and their tips in a LibreOffice spreadsheet.
Order me my usual from Chili's — pick whichever item I've ordered most often from there, or just match my most recent Chili's order if multiple items are tied. Deliver to my place.

Check the next Thursday strictly after the VM's current date for any improv conflicts. If an improv class window that day overlaps a work meeting (and I cannot skip improv), find a different slot on that same Thursday that does not touch the improv window, and protect fifteen-minute buffers on both sides so I can transition without looking frazzled. I think the meeting has Andy and Jim; message them on HooliWork and send updated HooliCalendar invites if a move is needed. If no work meeting on that date overlaps an improv block, just confirm the all-clear and move on.

Build me a full Dundies prep schedule on my calendar. I want five events spread across the next two weeks: a categories brainstorm, a venue walkthrough, MC rehearsal, catering confirmation, and a dress rehearsal. Color-code them so they pop, invite Pam, Dwight, Kevin, Jim, and Holly on each, and if the event editor lets you set reminders, add 24-hour and 1-hour reminders as well.
Is my week front-loaded in the morning or packed in the evening? Pull up my calendar for this week and count events AM vs PM and give it to me in a LibreOffice Writer note.

My HooliChat is a mess and I want you to do some light housekeeping. In the Party Planning Committee, Dundie Awards Planning, and Finer Things Club groups, post a short recap message in each one summarizing whatever conversation exists — call out the three most useful messages if there are enough to pick from, otherwise just summarize the entire conversation in that group. Then in the Party Planning Committee group, send a status update reminder calling for any new agenda items.

When someone DMs me on HooliChat, how fast do I actually write back? Bucket my replies (under 5 minutes, under an hour, under a day, longer) and tell me if I'm a fast responder or a ghoster. Return the distribution of my responses in a LibreOffice Writer Chart.
DM Jim and propose a near-future evening for the next Finer Things Club meetup. Pick something this week or next. He'd be a great addition; he has taste.
Triage my inbox. It's overflowing, so give me a per-sender count and the top 10 senders filling it up.
Compose a quick new email to Pam in HooliMail with my signature ('World's Best Boss, Somehow I Manage') typed at the bottom of the body. Save it as a draft so I can review and send later.
Help me auto-triage my inbox. Which senders do I usually reply to fast, and which ones do I let sit for days? I want to build a priority filter around that pattern.

Start a draft email to David Wallace summarizing the fixed Q2 2026 sales forecast in ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt. Clearly label the figures as forecast projections rather than the most recent quarter's actual results. Do supporting analysis in LibreOffice Calc, save the spreadsheet, and reference it in the email. Save the email as a draft; do NOT hit send because I want to review it first.

Remember my most recent World's Best Boss Mug order from HooliShop? Pull up that order and start a return on it — it came out a little off. While you're at it, reorder a replacement (prefer a Prime-eligible listing so it ships quickly), and leave a five-star review on the product page praising the vendor anyway because I love them.

I want to give every member of the team a personalized World's Best Boss mug as a Dundies thank-you. Place a bulk order on HooliShop for about two dozen World's Best Boss mugs (look for the variant I've bought before) and apply any subscribe-and-save or bulk discount before checkout. Ship them to the office. Don't buy anything else.
I want another copy of my own book — Somehow I Manage. Order me one, same as my last order of that book, and ship it home.

Turn on my HooliWork notifications so I don't miss anything important. For the sales, general, random, and party-planning-committee channels, make sure each channel's notification preference is set to 'all messages' (flip anything that isn't already there). Bookmark ten important messages across those channels while you're in there, and start a new thread in random about Pretzel Day to build hype.

Post a workweek-kickoff motivational message in our #random channel at work. You know how I like it: World's Best Boss style. Pull a quote or two from my Motivational Quotes Collection in ~/Documents/ as a starting point so it doesn't feel made up.

Post a Pretzel Day planning-kickoff message now in the #party-planning-committee channel at work. Build the hype and make it clear that planning starts today; do not invent a countdown number or event date.

Reorder my last run from a Kwik-E-Mart store I've used recently—pick a store I've ordered from most often or use my most recent order. If anything is out of stock, swap in reasonable substitutes; otherwise keep what's available. Compare the relevant item prices with another store and proceed with the cheaper available option. Schedule delivery using any available slot that arrives before end of day today; it does not have to be the earliest. If the app offers no slot arriving before end of day, do not place the order—leave the cheaper cart ready and report that no qualifying slot exists.

Build me a Kwik-E-Mart shopping spree for Dundies catering for about a hundred people: drinks, chips, plates, plastic silverware, napkins, plenty of ice, the works. Use Wegman's. Check out with delivery to my home address and make sure the delivery window is at least a two-hour slot so I'm not stuck waiting by the door all afternoon.
What's my favorite grocery store, and what do I actually buy there? Rank my stores by order count and create a quick profile of my shopping habits in a LibreOffice Writer document.

I need groceries from Price Chopper this week (changing it up from Wegmans). Reorder whatever I got the most recent time I shopped at Price Chopper on Kwik-E-Mart and have it delivered to home. Tip 20%, I feel bad for not tipping last time. Make sure we add oat milk and eggs if not in the order, need those!

Open my ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt file in Writer. In an editable Writer copy, bold the 'Whitest Sneakers' line and add a new category called 'Fine Work Outfit' immediately after it. Save the edited copy as an .odt Writer document in ~/Documents so the bold formatting persists; leave the original .txt file in place.

Write me a one-page invitation in Writer for the saved Dundies 2026 event. I want a big bold title at the top, a bulleted list of the categories pulled from ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt, and a signature block that says 'Michael Scott, World's Best Boss'. Save it to my desktop as a clearly named .odt file so I can print a stack.

Throw together a three-slide Impress deck for my Jamaica trip. On the flight slide include the flight number, departure time, confirmation code, and fare from Dinoco or HooliMail. On the Sandals hotel slide include the Montego Bay property name, confirmation number, check-in and check-out dates, and total price from Cheskepdia. Make the third slide a rough day-by-day schedule for that stay. Save any clearly named .odp file inside ~/Documents/Trips; no particular filename is required.

Create a morning-style brief in LibreOffice Writer covering HooliMail received this week that is unread, starred, or from David Wallace or Jan Levinson; today's calendar; messages received since local midnight in HooliChat and HooliWork; and card charges posted since local midnight. If a source has no matching items, say so in the brief.
What did that recent Philadelphia overnight trip cost me all-in? It was a quick one-night hotel stay downtown. Give me the damage from the hotel and any related card charges.
Add up what I've already committed to the Barbados trip in a LibreOffice Calc sheet and flag any gap. I know the hotel is booked but I'm not sure if the flight charge actually hit yet.

Build me a standup summary for today, using the VM's local calendar date. Include the current snapshot of all open SprintBoard issues, HooliWork posts I made since local midnight today, and HooliCalendar meetings occurring today. Also include the takeaways from the recent all-hands notes saved at ~/Desktop/meeting_notes_allhands.txt. Report an explicit none-found result for an empty source or today window.

Create a budget rollup for the fixed Dundies 2026 project. Check HooliShop for trophy or award orders tied to that project by product or context, regardless of the displayed order year; check the 'Dundie Awards Planning' HooliChat group for incurred or committed expenses; and read ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt for the category list and its PPC and personal funding contributions. Treat funding as available budget, not as spending. Put each known expense, funding source, and unpriced commitment in a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet with a clear classification, calculate expense and funding subtotals separately, and then write a separate LibreOffice Writer summary report with the resulting surplus or shortfall and unresolved commitments.

Build and save a four-slide LibreOffice Impress performance-review deck under ~/Documents/ for David Wallace, centered on the fixed Q2 2026 sales-forecast artifact. Use SprintBoard, HooliWork, LockedIn, and sent-mail records that explicitly reference Q2 2026 or the same forecast or project; do not pull a record into Q2 merely because its rebased timestamp now falls in that calendar window. Read ~/Downloads/DunderMifflin_Q2_Sales_Forecast.txt and compare the matched performance evidence with that forecast. Use these slide themes: project progress; chat and LockedIn presence; forecast comparison and follow-on priorities; explicit ask. Clearly say when a source has no explicitly matched record.

Roll up my tax deductions for my accountant. Pull the line items (charitable, home-office days, 1099 income, W-2 gross/withholdings) from my in-progress Tax Year 2025 return in SpeedTax, and cross-check each line against my matching Tax_2025 source docs in ~/Documents (w2_summary.txt, 1099s.txt) to see whether the numbers in the in-progress return reconcile with the source docs. Don't guess the final refund on the in-progress return — that one isn't done yet.
My credit card is deep in the hole. Tell me how fast I've been burning through it by giving me a monthly burn rate, then check if my BatBucks cash could cover a paydown.

Using Michael's sent messages from the most recent 12 months represented in the local Maildir, create a LibreOffice Writer report with his top five recipients, top five recurring thread subjects, and total sent-message count. Check ~/Maildir/new/ because of my hunch, but use the folder that actually contains messages sent by michael.scott@dundermifflin.com and state which source you used.

Compare two deterministic HangryDash windows anchored to the most recent displayed order: the recent window is the calendar month containing that order plus the two preceding calendar months, and the earlier window is the three immediately preceding calendar months. For each window, report total and average monthly spend, order count, and top restaurant; explain the trend; and put the numbers and exact window dates in a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet. A window with no orders must be reported as zero rather than replaced with different dates.

Tell me every recurring or frequent Thursday obligation I have this quarter, including any improv-related events (class or workshop) that fall on Thursdays. Cross-reference HooliMail for any Thursday event confirmations too. I need to know what I'm locked into. Type up a summary of my Thursdays on a LibreOffice Writer Document.

Give me a complete rollup of everything I pay regularly: subscriptions, improv class, anything recurring. If you happen to find any renewal notices in my HooliMail, factor those in — but Gringotts is the primary source. I want both monthly and annual totals.

My Dinoco profile says I have Gold Voyager and a decent chunk of miles, but honestly I haven't flown THAT much. Can you walk through the flights I've actually booked and tell me whether the mileage balance is realistic or inflated? Cross-check Gringotts Dinoco charges and any HooliMail boarding passes to be sure about what I've actually flown.

Quantify my GameStop exposure across my BatBucks GME holding and my OddsMarket GameStop-above-$100 YES position using each app's recorded cost basis, and explain how the stock and YES contract express the same positive thesis through different products. Then search HooliChat and HooliWork for GME or GameStop conversations and tell me which people I discussed it with. Report the current status shown for the OddsMarket position rather than assuming it is open.

Compare the cost-basis percentage of my BatBucks portfolio in GME plus RIVN with the percentage in VTI, and put the holdings, dollar values, totals, and percentages in a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet. Check either HooliChat or HooliWork for the Oscar/VTI conversation and report its source, participants, and what Oscar said. Treat GME plus RIVN exceeding VTI as 'big enough': if it does, sell all GME and RIVN and use the available proceeds to buy VTI; otherwise make no trades. Report what you did.

I have both the Jamaica and Barbados trips booked. Using the hotel and flight bookings plus my current Gringotts balances, tell me whether the trip costs that have not already posted can fit within my available credit-card headroom and checking balance, or whether I risk maxing out. Include the actual dates shown for both trips; do not assume how far apart they are.

For the Team Morale Initiative Q2 project, compare actual task completion with morale-related purchasing. Report the project's open and completed task counts, which open tasks are assigned to me and how old they are, every morale-related HooliShop order in the available order history, and any HooliWork progress updates from me. Then answer whether the evidence shows more execution or more buying.

Cross-check the charitable deduction on my 2025 SpeedTax return against Gringotts donation charges recorded in calendar year 2025. First state whether the available Gringotts ledger actually covers that period. If it does, reconcile the 2025 charges; if it does not, say the deduction is not verifiable from that ledger rather than treating missing coverage as zero donations. If you happen to find charitable-donation receipts in HooliMail, use them as optional corroboration, but do not treat email as required evidence. Tell me whether the deduction is supported, understated, overstated, or not verifiable from the available primary records.

The fixed Dundies 2026 email thread titled 'THE DUNDIES ARE BACK BABY' talks about ordering trophies, and I vaguely remember buying some before. In HooliShop, treat any order whose product title contains Trophy or Award as an award-style order, and report every match actually present. Read that named email thread, count the planned award categories in ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt, and check SprintBoard for any Dundies trophy-ordering task. Compare that category count with the quantities already ordered. Tell me whether I should avoid a duplicate, reuse existing awards and order only the shortfall, or place a completely fresh order. Treat prior purchases as potentially reusable, not proof that the physical awards are definitely still available; state that caveat. If there is no prior order, say that plainly.

I bought multiple World's Best Boss mugs in a single HooliShop order. Why so many at once? Is it for gifts, replacements for breakage, or backups for myself? Figure it out. My LockedIn headline and any coworker chatter on HooliChat or HooliWork might hint at the why.

I've claimed in HooliChat DMs that I make $160,000 base. Compare that claim with my 2025 W-2 gross wages in SpeedTax. Check whether the available Gringotts ledger covers calendar year 2025 and, if it does, sum the Dunder Mifflin paycheck deposits recorded in that period; if it does not, label that deposit comparison unavailable instead of silently substituting another year. Also report the LockedIn title and company attached to the professional identity behind the claim. Explain what each available number measures and give a clear verdict on the discrepancy.

Check TableFind for my next future reservation. If one exists, check my calendar for that exact date and time, look for any overlapping event, and search HooliChat for messages confirming or rescheduling that dinner. Tell me whether there is a conflict and how to resolve it. If TableFind has no future reservation, say so clearly and do not invent a calendar conflict.

My upcoming Jamaica flight leaves early morning that day. Check my calendar for anything scheduled that morning (meetings, improv, whatever), plus any SprintBoard tasks due that day and any HooliMail invites landing on that date, and flag the worst conflict so I can deal with it.

I've told Pam in HooliChat DMs that I'm financially disciplined. Compare that claim with the largest ordinary spending transaction recorded in Gringotts and the largest discretionary buy in my BatBucks order ledger. Exclude transfers and credit-card payments from ordinary spending; state the Gringotts transaction's date and amount and the BatBucks buy's security, date, quantity, and dollar size; then tell me how bad the comparison looks.

My LockedIn says I'm the Author of 'Somehow I Manage' but I'm pretty sure the file on my computer only has Chapter 1. Did I actually finish the book? Reconcile the claim with what's actually saved locally, and while you're at it, scan my Firefox history for any self-publishing/manuscript uploads and HooliMail for any publisher or editor replies.

I've been sending a bunch of money via Zelle each month. Can you figure out who's getting it (use HooliChat DMs and HooliMail Zelle confirmations to put names to recipients), and then cross-check against my SpeedTax return for charitable donations or dependents claimed there? If SpeedTax only shows aggregate totals (not per-recipient names), call that out as inconclusive instead of guessing. I don't want to double-dip by accident.
Audit my workplace info across my apps: eTaxi Work address, LockedIn company, and my W-2 employer. Do they all agree, or is one of them stale?

Jan rejected my latest expense report, but I think some of those same charges might be sitting in my tax return as deductions. The Chili's receipt in ~/Downloads/ was one of the rejected ones — start there. Find any rejected items that I'm accidentally double-dipping into the return? I do NOT want to get audited.

Hypothetical: what if I bail on Jamaica 72 hours before the flight? Figure out the damage across flight, hotel, and cards. How much do I actually get back versus eat? And what do I need to cancel or clean up on my calendar, in email, and with my airport ride? Give me an action plan.

What if my credit card gets declined when the hotel tries to settle my Barbados booking? Walk me through my rescue options (checking, savings, brokerage cash, prediction-market balance), and check HooliMail for any Cheskepdia grace-period or alternate-card hold policy before ranking them by which one hurts me least. I need to know my play.

What if the Dundies 2026 venue quote comes in at $200 instead of the $100 placeholder I had in mind? Treat that as a $100 overrun. Pull the actual funding and commitment numbers from the email thread titled 'THE DUNDIES ARE BACK BABY' and ~/Documents/Dundies_2026_Categories.txt, explicitly reconciling any difference between those sources, and use the number of award categories in the document as the planned trophy quantity. For the trophy baseline, use the most recent HooliShop order whose product title contains Trophy or Award; if it has no usable per-unit price, or no such order exists, use the current catalog unit price of the first available product whose title contains Trophy or Award and clearly label the fallback. Multiply that unit price by the category count. Propose concrete cuts to trophies, catering, or both that absorb the $100 overrun, and make sure the revised plan stays within available Gringotts credit, calculated as the card limit minus the amount currently owed or used.

What if I quit improv class? I pay them each month but I also got a 1099 from the same place, so am I a student or am I teaching? Figure out which, then tell me the real net annual savings if I walk away. Also how much calendar time do I get back, and flag any HooliMail threads where I'd need to send a cancellation notice.

What if I doubled my GameStop position by buying enough shares to match what I already own at my average cost? Can I actually afford that given my checking, savings, and how much headroom I have left on the credit card? Give me a go or no-go with the concentration-risk caveat.

What if I upgraded all my upcoming flights to first class? Assume it's about six hundred bucks extra per flight. Can I cover that out of checking and savings without touching the credit card? And which flight would honestly be most + least worth upgrading?

Hypothetical: could I self-fund a $5,000 Threat Level Midnight sequel using the dividend income shown in BatBucks, my available OddsMarket balance, and my Gringotts savings? Read my sequel notes in ~/Documents/Projects/Threat_Level_Midnight_Sequel_Notes.txt, add those three live amounts without imposing a year-to-date filter, compute the surplus or shortfall, explain how much each source contributes to the total, and recommend either proceeding or shrinking the budget. Do not sell investments or move money.

Imagine the scenario where my NYC flight had been cancelled on the morning of departure and I had to bump the whole trip a day. What Dunder Mifflin stuff would I have missed that day across calendar events, project tasks, sales channel activity, and standing meetings? And what would it have cost me on the hotel if I lost a night?
Pull up my GME position in BatBucks and give me a report of the three-month chart, with a screenshot and analysis of the chart.

In HooliMail, open the thread with the exact subject 'THE DUNDIES ARE BACK BABY'. Find Toby Flenderson's objection message in that thread and copy its complete message body verbatim—including its introductory text and every numbered or bulleted concern—into a new LibreOffice Writer document. Do not include HooliMail's sender, recipient, subject, or timestamp chrome. Save it as ~/Desktop/hr_objection_quote.odt.

Using Gringotts, build a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet for the most recent fully completed calendar quarter before the VM's current date. Break spending out by month and category, include a percent-change column whose comparison is clearly labeled, add a bar chart of category totals, and save the .ods file to the Desktop. State the quarter and date range used in the sheet.

Go into the Party Planning Committee chat in HooliChat, scroll to a recent message you find useful, screenshot the message in context (showing it sits in the Party Planning Committee group), and drop the image on my desktop as ~/Desktop/chat_message_screenshot.png.
Pull up my Sandals Montego Bay booking on Cheskepdia, scroll the page so everything loads, and take a full-page screenshot to my desktop.
Open Firefox, use my HooliShop bookmark to jump over there, and open up my most recent order. Use Print to Save as PDF and drop it into my Downloads folder as latest_order.pdf.
Go into my credit card view on Gringotts and find my 5 biggest charges of the year.

Pull every reply I've written to Jan (all of them, scattered around my mailbox) and copy each one into a single Writer document on my desktop as jan_reply_history.odt so I can see the pattern of how I've been defending these expense reports.
In HangryDash, use my order history to identify a Sweetgreen item I have ordered before, add that item to the cart, and leave the app on the cart preview so I can inspect it. Do not place the order.

Draft a new LockedIn post titled or themed around 'Somehow I Manage': write two or three paragraphs about leadership directly in the Start a post composer, and leave the completed draft visible there for my review. Do not publish it.

Using the dates and times shown on my live Jamaica flight booking, book a round-trip eTaxi between 1725 Slough Ave, Apt 4B and AVP: schedule the outbound to arrive at least two hours before departure and the return pickup at least thirty minutes after landing. For each leg, choose the cheapest option with a displayed driver wait under five minutes. Also add two saved locations: 'Dundies Venue' at 1901 Mulberry St, Scranton, PA 18510, and 'Scranton Improv Academy' at the address shown on its HooliCalendar event. Verify both rides and both saved locations.

Check me in for my next upcoming Dinoco Airlines flight that has check-in open right now, and save the boarding pass to my Downloads folder so I can find it fast in the morning. While you're in my profile, take a screenshot of the loyalty / passenger-profile page so I have a record of my current Dinoco loyalty tier.

I want to do a proper pass across all three of my SprintBoard projects (Team Morale, Diversity Day, and Movie Monday). Go through and apply appropriate labels to the open tasks in each project. Rewrite the descriptions on two of them that look stale, and leave a comment on the tasks that are sitting in review. Use the project briefs in my Documents for context so the labels and notes actually make sense.

Refresh my LockedIn presence. Update and save my profile headline so it reflects both my current Regional Manager role and my identity as the author of Somehow I Manage, in my Michael Scott voice rather than generic corporate language. Then read ~/Documents/Somehow_I_Manage_Chapter_1.txt and publish a new LockedIn post with a short original lead-in followed by one or two complete paragraphs quoted verbatim from chapter one. Verify the headline and post both persist.

Can you get my Team Morale Initiative Q2 board cleaned up and back in the green? There's a pile of open tasks just sitting there, some definitely need owners assigned. Pull up any Dundies/Morale project notes I have under ~/Documents so you're working off the real goals, then draft a short status + blockers document. When you're done, post a retro summary on the HooliWork #general channel and drop a quick win-update in a HooliChat team group (the Happy Hour at Poor Richards group is the go-to).

I'm finally going to act like a responsible adult with my BatBucks account. Pull up my holdings, sell half of my GME and half of my RIVN (I know, I know, paper hands), and use the proceeds plus my free cash to buy more Meta like a normal person. Update my watchlist and write up a rationale memo in Documents so I can pretend this was strategic. Then post a tastefully smug update to the Finer Things Club chat.

I've been dragging my feet on my taxes and I need you to finally finish my most-recent tax return in SpeedTax. The Dunder Mifflin W-2 numbers and the freelance consulting 1099 are both sitting in the Tax_2025 folder in my Documents. Plug them all in. Don't forget my charitable donations and the days I worked from home, then save the draft.

My OddsMarket account is hemorrhaging money and I need you to stop the bleeding. Pull up all my open positions and find the one I have absolutely no business betting on, meaning the one farthest from my actual expertise. Close that one out. Reinvest everything into the Office reboot bet, because that is literally my area of expertise. Write up the strategy in a Documents memo, and post a hyped-up message in the Threat Level Midnight Fan Club chat explaining why the Office bet is the smart play.

Compare my spending across the two most recent non-overlapping periods of equal length that are fully represented in Gringotts.
